methodologyNotes: Covers wired in-ear monitors (IEMs) — in-ear earphones sold to consumers, musicians, and audiophiles primarily for wired listening — with a published US MSRP or typical street price in USD. Includes single- and multi-driver models across dynamic, balanced-armature, planar-magnetic, electrostatic, and hybrid/tribrid topologies. Excludes true-wireless earbuds (see wireless-earbuds), open-ear/bone-conduction models, and custom-molded (CIEM) commissions; universal-fit versions of pro monitors are included. Price is US MSRP at launch, or typical street price where no formal MSRP exists, in USD. driverType is the overall topology enum: 'dynamic' | 'balanced-armature' | 'planar-magnetic' | 'electrostatic' | 'hybrid' | 'tribrid'. driverConfig is the per-earpiece driver complement as published, using DD (dynamic driver), BA (balanced armature), planar, and EST (electrostatic) — e.g. '1DD', '2DD+4BA', 'single planar'. impedanceOhms is rated nominal impedance in ohms (Ω) at 1 kHz. sensitivityDbMw is rated sensitivity in dB SPL per milliwatt (dB/mW) at 1 kHz; null when the manufacturer publishes only dB/Vrms. frequencyResponseHz is the manufacturer-published response range as a 'low-high' string in Hz. connectorType is the detachable-cable connector enum: '2pin-0.78mm' | 'mmcx' | 'qdc' | 'a2dc' | 'pentaconn-ear' | 'fixed' (non-detachable, hardwired cable). cableDetachable is a boolean (true if the cable can be swapped by the user). plugTermination is the included/primary source plug enum: '3.5mm' | '4.4mm' | '2.5mm' | 'usb-c' | 'modular' (swappable plug system). shellMaterial is the primary shell/faceplate material as published: e.g. 'resin' | 'acrylic' | 'aluminum' | 'stainless-steel' | 'titanium' | 'zinc-alloy' | 'liquid-metal'. weightGrams is the mass of a single earpiece in grams without cable; null when not disclosed.

products.name: Moondrop Blessing 3
products.priceNote: ShenzhenAudio (authorized retailer) lists both Regular price and Sale price as "$359.99 USD" for the "MOONDROP BLESSING 3 2DD 4BA In-Ear Headphone" (same 2DD+4BA model). The MOONDROP official page publishes no price. No formal US MSRP was fetched; $359.99 USD is the sourced typical street price.
products.provenance: The MOONDROP official product page (moondroplab.com/en/products/blessing3) confirms the exact model "Blessing3 Hybrid In-ear Monitor" with a 2DD+4BA driver complement, impedance 14.8Ω±15% (@1kHz), frequency response 10Hz-30kHz, sensitivity 120dB/Vrms (@1kHz), 3.5mm single-ended jack, 0.78-2pin detachable connector, and a housing of 3D-printed imported medical resin. ShenzhenAudio (authorized retailer) corroborates every one of these specs verbatim for the identical model and lists the price as $359.99 USD. Sensitivity is published only in dB/Vrms so sensitivityDbMw is null, and neither page discloses single-earpiece weight, so weightGrams is null.

products.name: Truthear Nova
products.priceNote: US price $169.99 listed verbatim on both the official TRUTHEAR product page ("$169.99 USD") and the SHENZHENAUDIO retailer page ("Regular price $169.99 USD" / "NOVA - $169.99") for the base NOVA configuration.
products.provenance: The official TRUTHEAR product page (truthear.com/products/nova) confirms this exact model as the NOVA 1DD+4BA in-ear monitor and lists $169.99 USD, sensitivity 123dB/Vrms @1KHz, frequency response 8-40kHz (IEC61094), a PU+LCP dynamic-driver diaphragm, a "0.78 2Pin" interchangeable cable, and a medical-grade high-transparency resin DLP-3D-printed cavity. The SHENZHENAUDIO retailer page corroborates the same NOVA 1DD+4BA model at $169.99 USD and additionally publishes impedance 14.8Ω±15% (@1kHz) and the hybrid topology ("NOVA Hybrid In-ear Monitor"). Sensitivity is published only in dB/Vrms (not dB/mW), so sensitivityDbMw is null; plug termination, single-earpiece weight, and a release date are not disclosed on either fetched page, so those are null.

products.name: Sennheiser IE 600
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP. SoundGuys review lists Price "Original: $699" with "Product release date: March 8, 2022"; Audio46 launch review (Jun 24, 2022) cites "($699)". Note: the Sennheiser US store currently lists $899.95, and the SoundGuys sidebar also shows a later "MSRP: USD799.95" — but the launch figure per methodology (MSRP at launch) is $699.
products.provenance: The official Sennheiser US product page (title "IE 600", article number/SKU 508948) confirms the exact model and its full specification table: single 7 mm TrueResponse dynamic driver ("Single Dynamic Driver, Pressure Chamber"), 4 – 46,500 Hz, 18 Ω, 118 dB at 1 kHz / 1 Vrms SPL, detachable Fidelity (+) MMCX connectors, and the 3D-printed AMLOY-ZR01 amorphous-metal housing. The SoundGuys review (Model Number "IE 600") corroborates the identity and supplies the launch price ("Original: $699"), the release date ("March 8, 2022"), and the per-earpiece weight ("6g (per earbud)"), consistent with the manufacturer specs. priceUsd is the 2022 US launch MSRP of $699; sensitivityDbMw is left null because Sennheiser publishes SPL only in dB per 1 Vrms, not dB/mW.

products.name: Shure SE846 Gen 2
products.priceNote: US MSRP $899, per Shure's official press release (Sept 15, 2022): the SE846 Gen 2 earphones "are available at ... select retailers for $899 (US), while the True Wireless Adapter soft bundle is available for $999 (US)." The $999 figure shown by some retailers (e.g., Thomann) is the TW Adapter bundle, not the standalone earphones.
products.provenance: Shure's official press release (source, dated September 15, 2022) confirms the model as the "SE846 Gen 2" — the second generation of the SE846 in Clear/Jade/Graphite — and states the US MSRP as $899 for the earphones (the $999 being the separate True Wireless Adapter soft bundle), with a September 15, 2022 launch. Thomann's retailer listing (corroboration) for the identical "Shure SE846 Gen 2" supplies the numeric spec table verbatim: impedance 9 Ohm at 1 kHz, sensitivity 114 dB SPL/mW at 1 kHz, frequency range 15 - 20,000 Hz, removable cable, and a gold-plated 3.5 mm jack. Driver topology (four balanced armature drivers) and the MMCX connector were verified verbatim on Shure's own product page (SKU SE846G2GT) and a dated ecoustics review, confirming this is the exact Gen 2 model and not the original SE846 or the TW bundle.

products.name: Sony IER-Z1R
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP $1,999.99, sourced verbatim from the Headfonics review (Ruji Abat, June 16 2019): "It retails for $1,999.99." (also shown as "$1999.99"). Sony's official page lists only MRP Rs. 169,990 (INR), so the USD figure is taken from the dated review. Current street price is lower (~$1,699–1,700 per OHHIFI/Headphones.com), but the formal launch MSRP is used per the category methodology.
products.provenance: The Sony official specifications page (sony.co.in) confirms the exact model "IER-Z1R Signature Series In-Ear Headphones" and supplies the verbatim specs used here: Hybrid type, 40 ohms impedance (1 kHz), 103 dB/mW sensitivity, 3–100,000 Hz frequency response, Detachable Y-type cord, approx. 26 g weight without cable, and included stereo-mini (3.5mm) + 4.4mm balanced plugs. The Headfonics dated review (June 16 2019) independently confirms the same IER-Z1R and states the US retail price verbatim ("It retails for $1,999.99."), plus the MMCX connectors, zirconium-alloy shell, and 3.5mm single-ended / 4.4mm balanced terminations, and situates the model in Sony's 2018 One Sound Signature Series launch. driverConfig is left null because neither cited page states the driver complement in the catalog's DD/BA digit form (Sony describes the three drivers in prose; Headfonics writes "dual DD and single BA"), though driverType="hybrid" is explicit on the Sony page.

products.name: 7Hz Timeless II
products.priceNote: US $229.00. Linsoul (authorized 7Hz distributor) product page, forced to USD, lists "Regular price $229.00 USD"; corroborated by the Audio46 review (Mar 6, 2025), which states the Timeless II is "priced at an accessible $229."
products.provenance: The Linsoul product page (7Hz's authorized distributor store) confirms this is the exact "7HZ Timeless II" with the upgraded 14.5mm planar magnetic driver, and its Technical Details table supplies impedance 15.2Ω, sensitivity 108dB/V @ 1kHz, 0.78mm 2-pin connector, and 5g per earbud; forcing the page to USD shows a Regular price of $229.00 USD. The Audio46 dated review (published Mar 6, 2025) independently confirms the same model and identical specs and states the price as "$229," and describes the swappable 3.5mm/4.4mm terminations included in the box. Frequency response was left null because the two pages disagree (Linsoul "20–20kHz" vs Audio46 "5 Hz–40kHz") and neither expresses it in plain Hz; sensitivity and shell material are null because both pages publish sensitivity only in dB/V (not dB/mW) and never name the shell material.

products.name: Meze Alba
products.priceNote: US price $159. Meze Audio official product page (International/USD store) lists "Sale price $159"; Bloom Audio, a US authorized Meze retailer, lists "Regular price $159.00" (variant price 15900 cents). The lower "$139" figures on Bloom are Open Box only.
products.provenance: The Meze Audio official product page (mezeaudio.com/products/alba) confirms this exact model — the ALBA single 10.8 mm dynamic-driver IEM — via its SPECIFICATIONS table (Transducer Type Dynamic, Sensitivity 109 dB SPL/mW at 1 kHz, Impedance 32 Ω, Frequency Range 15 Hz - 25 kHz, 2-pin 0.78 mm connectors with 3.5 mm gold-plated jack) and shows "Sale price $159" on the International (USD) store. Bloom Audio, a US authorized Meze retailer, corroborates both identity and price with "Regular price $159.00" and matching specs (10.8mm Dynamic Driver, 2-Pin | 3.5mm plug, 32Ω, 15 Hz-25 kHz), and explicitly states "Zinc alloy die-casted shells with anodized Aluminum parts," which fixes the shell as zinc-alloy and confirms the detachable 2-pin cable. Both pages agree on the same model and the $159 US price.

products.name: Etymotic ER4XR
products.priceNote: US launch MSRP $349. Sourced from Headfonics review (Jan 4, 2017), verbatim: "In 2016, Etymotic decided to relaunch the ER4 and offers two new products for consumers: The new SR ... and the XR ... at 349 $ each." Note: the current Etymotic manufacturer store page lists the price as "$ 309.99".
products.provenance: The Etymotic manufacturer product page (etymotic.com/product/er4xr-earphones) confirms this exact ER4XR model via its Technical Specs block: single high-performance balanced-armature driver per channel, 45 Ohms @ 1kHz impedance, 98 dB @ 1kHz/1mW sensitivity, 20 Hz–16 kHz frequency response, a detachable 5 ft cable with MMCX connectors terminating in a 3.5mm gold-plated stereo plug, and CNC-machined anodized-aluminum shells; the page shows a current store price of "$ 309.99". The Headfonics review (Jan 4, 2017) corroborates the identical spec table and states the ER4 was relaunched in 2016 with the SR and XR "at 349 $ each," establishing the $349 US launch MSRP. Both pages unambiguously identify the ER4XR (eXtended Response, added bass) variant as distinct from the flat-tuned ER4SR sibling that shares the cable and body but differs in bass tuning.

products.name: 64 Audio U12t
products.priceNote: US price $1,999.00 listed verbatim on the official 64 Audio product page (64audio.com/products/u12t): "$1,999.00 USD" for the U12t Universal Fit, 12 Drivers. HeadAmp corroborates model identity and specs but shows the item out of stock ("Join Waitlist") with no active price displayed.
products.provenance: The official 64 Audio product page (source) confirms this exact model — "U12t", Universal Fit, 12 Drivers — priced at "$1,999.00 USD", with specifications: 12 balanced-armature drivers (1 tia High, 1 High-Mid, 6 Mid, 4 Low), 12.6 Ω impedance, 108 dB/mW @ 1 kHz sensitivity, 10 Hz–20 kHz frequency response, 0.78mm 2-Pin detachable cables (3.5mm + 4.4mm), and a T6061 aluminum shell with electroformed stainless-steel faceplate. The HeadAmp retailer page (corroboration) independently confirms the U12t identity and matching specs: "Twelve precision balanced armature drivers", "1 tia high, 1 high-mid, 6 mid, 4 low", 12.6 Ω, 108 dB/mW, 10 Hz–20 kHz, and a detachable 1.2m cable with 3.5mm angled jack. Price is taken from the manufacturer page; HeadAmp lists the unit out of stock with no active price.

products.name: HIFIMAN RE2000 Pro
products.priceNote: US MSRP $2,000. HIFIMAN's official product page (RE2000 PRO Gold, hifiman.com/products/detail/316) lists price "$2000"; authorized US dealer Sound Approach independently lists "Your Price: $2,000.00" for the RE2000 Pro Gold. This applies to the flagship gold-plated variant; a lower-priced RE2000 Pro Silver (aviation-grade aluminum shell) also exists, so $2,000 is specifically the Gold.
products.provenance: HIFIMAN's official product page (detail/316) identifies the exact model as "RE2000 PRO Gold" and publishes Frequency Response 5Hz-20kHz, Impedance 60Ω, Sensitivity 103dB, and price "$2000". Authorized US dealer HiFiSoundGear's RE2000 PRO Gold page corroborates the same electrical specs plus the Topology Diaphragm 9.2mm single dynamic driver, a 24k gold-plated housing, and box contents that include a detachable "2-Pin 3.5mm Cable" with Dual Pin connectors (hence cableDetachable true, plugTermination 3.5mm). Both pages confirm this is the RE2000 Pro Gold flagship at $2,000; connectorType (2-pin pitch not stated), shellMaterial (gold plating is not an enum material and the base metal is not published), weightGrams and releaseDate were left null as no fetched Pro-Gold page states them verbatim.
